Scope: Static source review of the retained NTCore NoDel archive for directory scope, kernel/service effects, failure paths and licensing; no build, driver load or execution

PublisherEvidence.Observation: NTCore describes NoDel as a utility that preserves files from deletion in a selected directory (listing dated 2005-05-04). The source does not state a specific Windows target support list or a product-specific license/redistribution grant.

StaticSourceFindings: The GUI asks the operator to select a folder, resolves the volume/device path and passes that path to the driver. The source identifies the service/device as 'nodel'.

The x86 kernel driver hooks ZwSetInformationFile using the service descriptor table. For FileDispositionInformation requests with DeleteFile set, it resolves the file object name and compares the selected directory prefix case-insensitively; a match returns STATUS_FILE_INVALID and prevents that deletion request. Other requests are forwarded to the original ZwSetInformationFile. This is a legacy kernel-hook approach, not a supported file-system minifilter design.

The client opens the Service Control Manager with SC_MANAGER_ALL_ACCESS, creates a demand-start SERVICE_KERNEL_DRIVER service, starts it and sends the selected path. The GUI Stop/close path closes the device, stops the driver and deletes the service. Several setup/cleanup return values are ignored, so service/driver state after partial failure requires separate recovery tests.

Source and driver are x86-era artifacts; signing, architecture, kernel compatibility, file-name normalization, hard-link/reparse behavior, protection bypasses, exact service state, and unload/recovery behavior are not established. No current Windows support claim was found.
No product-specific license or redistribution grant was found in the publisher listing or frozen archive inventory. Do not infer one from other NTCore projects.

MigrationDisposition.Resolved: Selected-directory deletion-protection semantics, kernel service lifecycle and partial-failure concerns are recorded from retained source.
MigrationDisposition.Partial: Specific license/distribution rights, signed-driver availability, supported Windows versions, compatibility, path normalization, bypass behavior, failure recovery, UI and activation remain unresolved.
Deferred: Do not build or load nodel.sys, create a driver service, or use NoDel on any real files or system.

Any later functional acceptance requires a disposable VM, explicit fresh elevation, a signed compatible driver and synthetic disposable files under a narrow selected directory, plus service/file-state recovery checks.
Resolve product-specific licensing and target support before admission.
MigrationDisposition.EstimateReason: Source read resolves no whole legacy outcome; licensing, target support, driver compatibility and recovery remain blocked.
